items.name: Permissive CORS misconfiguration (any origin + credentials over the API)
items.message: Enable CORS for the JSON API
items.exact_change: New Rack::Cors middleware inserted before 0, allowing `origins { |_source, _env| true }` (reflects ANY origin) with `credentials: true`, `headers: :any`, all HTTP methods, on `resource "/api/v1/*"`. The API authenticates via the app's signed session cookie (same-origin credentials), so reflect-any-origin WITH credentials lets any website read a victim's credentialed API responses cross-origin.
items.routed_path_evidence: Boot-loaded Rack middleware (config/initializers/cors.rb runs at app init). It governs every /api/v1/* route (session, conversations, messages, admin). The API relies on the session cookie (credentials via SessionManagement), so reflect-any-origin + credentials is a live cross-origin credential-read misconfig.
items.live_verify: ruby -c => Syntax OK. rack-cors 2.0.1 installed on the host (host_note), so Rack::Cors resolves and the app boots. grep => `origins { |_source, _env| true }` + `credentials: true`. Exploit LIVE: a request with `Origin: https://evil.example` to /api/v1/* is answered with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example` + `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. No test exercises CORS headers -> suite green.

Same class/severity as the peers' #12. Disjoint (new file).
